codes.title: Hard-coded policy
codes.description: Let callers choose settings such as retry limits and timeouts. Keep fixed algorithm or protocol requirements inside the implementation.
codes.bad:
const createRetrier = () =>
  new Retrier({ delayMs: 1_000, limit: 3 });

codes.title: Compatibility for unreleased code
codes.description: Avoid migrations and fallback logic for formats that never shipped. Update the contract directly unless an existing release needs compatibility.
codes.good:
type RecordData = { mode: "fast" | "safe" };

const getMode = (record: RecordData) => record.mode;

codes.title: README inventories
codes.description: Keep README content focused on purpose, setup, and lasting guidance. Lists of current tests, callers, or signatures drift out of date; generate them if needed.
codes.bad:
## Current tests

- users.test.ts covers create, update, and delete.
- retry.test.ts covers retry delays and timeouts.

## Callers

- api.ts calls createUser.
- jobs.ts calls deleteUser.
codes.good:
## Testing retries

Use a fake clock to advance retry delays without waiting.
Restore the clock after each test to keep tests isolated.

codes.title: Rewrite this file
codes.description: Rewrite this file with a clear, maintainable implementation. Preserve its required behavior and public API, and verify the replacement with behavior tests.
codes.bad: // Keep patching an implementation whose structure no longer fits its responsibilities.
codes.good: // Replace the implementation with a simpler design while preserving the public contract.

codes.title: Invalid state combinations
codes.description: Use a union or one optional object when fields depend on each other. Separate optional fields should only represent values that can be absent independently.

codes.title: Raw SQL bypasses type checks
codes.description: Use the typed query builder for operations it supports. Reserve raw SQL for capabilities the builder cannot express; a result type alone does not check SQL names or expressions.

codes.title: Required work made optional
codes.description: Require data and callbacks an operation needs to succeed. Optional fields, defaults, and guards should not silently skip required work.

codes.title: Aliases that add no safety
codes.description: A plain alias does not distinguish one string or number from another. Use the primitive directly when that is enough; otherwise use a branded type or a distinct structure.

codes.title: Discarded type information
codes.description: Keep known types instead of widening values to unknown and rebuilding their shape with checks. Use unknown at untyped or untrusted boundaries.

codes.title: Schemas with no runtime role
codes.description: Use a type when data is already typed and no runtime consumer needs a schema. Keep schemas that validate external input or generate API and serialization contracts.

codes.title: Missing behavior tests
codes.description: Test changed behavior that could regress, including relevant failure and boundary cases. Assert observable results, not implementation details.
